prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (ideological framing removed)

- Economy and business: Responsible public finances; industrial strategy focused on green, digital and biosciences; expand British Business Bank; reverse bank tax cuts; increase Digital Services Tax to 6%; fairer capital gains tax; 4% levy on FTSE‑100 share buybacks; windfall tax on oil and gas profits; target future income tax cuts by raising personal allowance; abolish business rates and replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy; 3% of GDP for R&D by 2030; prompt payment enforcement; local banking; AI regulatory framework; gigabit broadband nationwide; consumer digital literacy target.

- Jobs and work: Replace apprenticeship levy with a flexible skills levy; guarantee apprentices at least the National Minimum Wage; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants for adults; new “dependent contractor” status; 20% higher minimum wage for zero‑hours workers at normal demand; right to request fixed hours after 12 months; overhaul SSP (eligibility, rate, day‑one pay, small employer support); Worker Protection Enforcement Authority; living wage review.

- Climate, energy and environment: Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; 10‑year home upgrades with free insulation and heat pumps for low‑income households; zero‑carbon standard for all new buildings now; rooftop solar incentives and fair export price; social energy tariff; decouple electricity from gas price; ban fracking and new coal; expand storage and interconnectors; enable community energy; carbon border adjustment; associate UK ETS with EU ETS; citizens’ assemblies; targets to “double nature” by 2050; 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act and new Air Quality Agency; end sewage discharges, transform water companies into public‑benefit firms, tougher regulator and “sewage tax”; deposit return scheme; phase out non‑recyclable single‑use plastics within three years; protect 30% land/sea by 2030.

- Health and care: Right to see a GP in seven days/24h if urgent; 8,000 more GPs; expand pharmacists’ roles and 24/7 booking; NHS dentistry access and contract reform; youth mental health hubs and school professionals; mental health check‑ups; cancer treatment start within 62 days; upgrade radiotherapy; Cancer Survival Research Act; ten‑year NHS retention and capital plans; ambulance handover fixes; Patients’ Charter; digital interoperability; legal, regulated cannabis market (18+, potency limits); Infected Blood compensation. Social care: free personal care; workforce plan; Royal College of Care Workers; Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/h); unpaid carers’ paid leave, respite, higher allowance; National Care Agency; portable care packages; tech‑enabled care; Commissioner for Older People; kinship care support.

- Education and families: Per‑pupil funding above inflation; clear school repairs backlog; tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils; mental health professional in every school (funded by higher DST); extra free hours and higher Early Years Pupil Premium; teacher workforce strategy and independent pay body; SEND national body; Young People’s Premium (16–18); restore maintenance grants; Erasmus Plus return; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants. Families: free school meals for all children in poverty (aim: all primary); parental leave/pay day‑one rights incl. self‑employed; double SMP/SPP to £350/week; paternity at 90% pay and an extra month; neonatal leave; “Toddler Top‑Up”.

- Welfare and pensions: Scrap two‑child limit and benefit cap; target ending deep poverty; UC first payment in five days; scrap bedroom tax; replace sanctions with incentive‑based support; protect triple lock; WASPI compensation; increase Carer’s Allowance and eligibility; disability assessment reforms; tackle gender pension gap.

- Housing: Build 380,000 homes/year incl. 150,000 social; 10 garden cities; zero‑carbon new homes; retrofit programme; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; ban no‑fault evictions; three‑year default tenancies; national landlord register; council powers to end Right to Buy; rent‑to‑own for social housing; remove unsafe cladding at no cost to leaseholders; end rough sleeping next Parliament; controls on second homes/short‑lets; “use‑it‑or‑lose‑it” permissions.

- Transport: Restore 2030 zero‑emission sales date; mass EV charging rollout, 5% VAT on public charging, card access, plug‑in grant; freeze rail fares, simplify ticketing; new Railway Agency; Northern Powerhouse Rail; rail electrification plan; bus franchising powers and £2 cap during review; active travel networks; more local road maintenance; zero‑carbon flight R&D; private‑jet super‑tax; ban short domestic flights where rail <2.5h; moratorium on net airport expansion.

- Crime and justice: Community policing; police attendance guarantee for all burglaries; Online Crime Agency; scrap Police and Crime Commissioners; halve offence‑to‑sentence times; domestic abuse specialists; targeted mental‑health response; fraud reimbursement; EU cooperation; modern slavery enforcement; reduce overcrowding; women’s justice board; resettlement plan.

- Immigration and asylum: End Hostile Environment; move work‑visa policy out of Home Office; scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; 3‑month service standard for asylum decisions; right to work after 3 months; expand safe/legal routes (resettlement, humanitarian permits, family reunion); flexible, merit‑based work visas; exempt NHS/care staff from skills charge; reverse family‑visa income hike; expand Youth Mobility; automatic Settled Status for EU pre‑settled; Windrush redress; repeal Right to Rent; firewall for public services.

- Rights and governance: Uphold Human Rights Act and ECHR; Race Equality Strategy; make misogyny a hate crime; ban conversion practices; repeal recent anti‑protest laws; Digital Bill of Rights and biometric safeguards; expand VAWG services; reproductive healthcare protections; gender recognition reform incl. non‑binary; disability employment support; assisted‑dying free vote. Political reform: PR (STV) for MPs and English councils; votes at 16; cap donations; Lords reform; federal constitution; citizens’ assemblies; stronger transparency and lobbying rules; Hillsborough Law.

- Defence and foreign policy: Increase defence spending towards 2.5% GDP; reverse Army cuts; maintain nuclear deterrent; parliamentary vote before military action; tighter arms‑export controls; improve personnel housing, pay and support; deepen European and Five Eyes security cooperation. International: rebuild EU ties via staged roadmap (incl. veterinary agreements; Single Market aim); support Ukraine incl. using seized Russian assets; restore 0.7% aid with poverty/climate/education focus; fund BBC World Service; recognise Palestine and pursue two‑state solution with immediate ceasefire; targeted human‑rights sanctions; measures on China (Uyghurs genocide recognition, BNO support).
